props.title: The Easter Bunny Is Comin' to Town

sections.content: This Rankin/Bass stop-motion animation special follows the pattern established by their Christmas classics like Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer (1964) and Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town (1970). Fred Astaire returns as a mailman narrator (S.D. Kluger), explaining the origins of Easter traditions through the story of Sunny, an orphan bunny who brings joy to the gloomy town of Town. Like many Rankin/Bass productions, it combines whimsical character design with catchy musical numbers and an origin story format that explains holiday traditions to children.

sections.content: The late 1970s marked a golden age for holiday-themed animation specials, with Rankin/Bass leading the charge. Their signature Animagic stop-motion style, developed in Japan with MOM Production, gave these specials a distinctive look that influenced holiday programming for decades. The Year Without a Santa Claus (1974) and Jack Frost (1979) showcased similar world-building approaches, creating interconnected holiday mythologies that explained familiar customs through creative origin stories.

The special's message about bringing joy through generosity and overcoming bureaucratic obstacles reflects common themes in children's entertainment of the 1970s. Like 'Twas the Night Before Christmas (1974), another Rankin/Bass production, it emphasizes community cooperation and the power of tradition. The character designs by Paul Coker Jr. maintain the studio's characteristic style while adding Easter-specific flourishes. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

sections.content: While not as widely remembered as Rankin/Bass Christmas specials, "The Easter Bunny Is Comin' to Town" established important templates for holiday origin stories in animation. Its influence can be seen in later works like Rise of the Guardians (2012), which similarly reimagined holiday figures as heroic characters. The special's mix of musical numbers, origin story elements, and child-friendly conflict resolution became standard features of holiday entertainment.
